title: National Council of Social Service (Amendment) Bill
what_it_is: National Council of Social Service (Amendment) Bill

sections.label: MSF funding for NCSS
sections.summary: MSF funding for social service programmes doubled from $172 million in FY2014 to $346 million in FY2024, with full funding for NCSS core functions since 2022.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: In addition, MSF's funding for social service programmes has doubled in the last decade from $172 million dollars in financial year (FY)2014 to $346 million dollars in FY2024.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: To ensure that NCSS is adequately resourced to fulfil this expanded role, the Government has progressively increased its funding over the years, particularly by providing full funding for NCSS' core functions since 2022.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: To share some examples: NCSS set up the Community Capability Trust in 2020 to strengthen the organisations that deliver services, including helping SSAs adopt digital technologies that improve the quality and efficiency of their services.

sections.label: Engagements on the Bill
sections.summary: About 300 NCSS member organisations and members of the public were engaged to shape this Bill.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: To shape this Bill, we conducted extensive engagements with about 300 NCSS member organisations and members of the public.

sections.label: Disability and Inclusion Panel Study
sections.summary: NCSS launched the Disability and Inclusion Panel Study in 2022 to understand experiences and needs of persons with disabilities and their caregivers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: For instance, NCSS launched the Disability and Inclusion Panel Study in 2022 to understand the experiences and needs of persons with disabilities and their caregivers, which informs Singapore's broader strategy for disability inclusion.

sections.label: Sector membership in clause 10
sections.summary: Clause 10 introduces sector membership, a single-tier membership framework for organisations in the sector, following the change in NCSS' constitution.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: With the change in NCSS' constitution, clause 10 introduces sector membership, a single-tier membership framework for organisations in the sector to complement NCSS' sector developer role.

sections.label: Fees for sector membership
sections.summary: Member organisations are charged nominal membership fees today, but fees will not be charged for sector membership.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: Member organisations are charged nominal membership fees today.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: However, fees will not be charged for sector membership.

sections.label: Full Council members transition
sections.summary: All Full Council members, who make up the majority of NCSS' membership today, will be transitioned to become sector members.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: All Full Council members, who make up the majority of NCSS' membership today, will be transitioned to become sector members.

sections.label: NCSS Board employee restrictions
sections.summary: The current restrictions on the NCSS Board will be removed to allow employees of sector members to sit on the Council.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: To this end, we will move away from the current restrictions applicable to the NCSS Board and allow employees of sector members to sit on the Council.

sections.label: Council size and term
sections.summary: The Council will have a maximum of 27 members and a minimum of 15, with a maximum term of three years.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: The Council will comprise a maximum of 27 members and a minimum of 15, with a maximum term of three years.

sections.label: ComChest role and governance changes
sections.summary: Clause 7 extends ComChest's role beyond fundraising to mobilising other resources, and includes modernising the Act's language, financial provisions, governance clauses, honorarium payments, and NCSS reclassification.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: Clause 7 provides that ComChest's role extends beyond fundraising to include mobilising other resources, such as volunteers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: This includes modernising the language and structure of the Act, such as updating the financial provisions, strengthening clauses relating to the governance of the Council, ComChest and NCSS' committees to maintain high standards of conduct; providing for Council members to be paid an honorarium in line with the PSD's guidelines; and reclassifying NCSS as a Group 1A public body in the First Schedule to the Public Sector (Governance) Act 2018, similar to other Statutory Boards that play sector developer roles.

sections.label: Debate key themes and significant change
sections.summary: The debate will focus on a few key themes, and this part of the Bill represents the most significant change from current practice for the sector.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong Central)
sentences.text: The debate will focus on a few key themes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong Central)
sentences.text: This is the part of the Bill that represents the most significant change from current practice for the sector.

sections.label: Compliance burden for smaller organisations
sections.summary: Second, compliance burden, especially for smaller member organisations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong Central)
sentences.text: Second, compliance burden, especially for smaller member organisations.

sections.label: Consultation process and Board size
sections.summary: NCSS and MSF are commended for a thorough and extensive consultation process, exemplified by NCSS expanding the Board size range after consultation with the sector.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong Central)
sentences.text: Beyond the substance of the debate on this Bill, let me conclude by making a point on the process that has undergirded this Bill.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong Central)
sentences.text: And here, I wish to commend NCSS and MSF, for undertaking a really thorough and extensive consultation process with the sector and stakeholders.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong Central)
sentences.text: The best example of this is NCSS' decision to expand the range of the Board size after consultation with the sector.

sections.label: Council member number range
sections.summary: Section 5(1) sets Council members at 15 to 27, up from a previous upper limit of 23, prompting a request for rationale.

sentences.speaker: Prof Kenneth Poon (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Section 5, sub-section 1 provides for the number of Council members to range from 15 to 27.

sentences.speaker: Prof Kenneth Poon (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: That is compared with a previous upper limit of 23.

sentences.speaker: Prof Kenneth Poon (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Given the increasing complexity of responsibilities within NCSS, I would appreciate some clarification on the rationale for providing this wider range.

sentences.speaker: Prof Kenneth Poon (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In particular, it will be helpful to understand the circumstances under which such a larger Council would be required and how these flexibilities are intended to support effective representation, expertise and governance of a more complex sector.

sections.label: NCSS statutory functions expansion
sections.summary: The NCSS (Amendment) Bill expands NCSS' statutory functions as a system steward of the social service sector.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: The NCSS (Amendment) Bill formally expands NCSS' statutory functions as a system steward of the social service sector.

sections.label: Functions in the Bill
sections.summary: The Bill provides for functions including advising Government, coordinating social service provision, setting standards, building capability, mobilising resources and supporting national social policy.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: The Bill expressly provides for functions such as advising Government, coordinating social service provision, setting standards, building sector capability, mobilising resources and supporting the implementation of national social policy.

sections.label: Council sector-wide data role
sections.summary: The Bill clarifies the Council's role in collecting, analysing and using sector-wide data for planning, evaluation and research.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: The Bill also clarifies the Council's role in collecting, analysing and using sector-wide data for planning, evaluation and research, building on improved digital and data capabilities.

sections.label: Over-centralisation risk warning
sections.summary: A stronger NCSS can improve coherence and coordination but, if not carefully calibrated, may lead to unintended over-centralisation.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: A stronger NCSS can improve coherence coordination, but if it is not carefully calibrated, it may also lead to unintended over-centralisation of decision-making, resources and influence.

sections.label: Governance and data obligations
sections.summary: The Bill's strengthened governance and data obligations may increase reporting, audits and evaluation requirements.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: The Bill's strengthened governance and data obligations may increase reporting, audits and evaluation requirements.

sections.label: Charity audit and compliance costs
sections.summary: Charities already spend significantly on internal and external audits, procurement systems and compliance, costing money, manpower and administrative effort.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: From experience, the charities I serve already incur significant expenditures on internal audits and external audits, procurement systems and compliance processes – costs that involve not just financial outlays, but also substantial manpower and administrative effort.

sections.label: Volunteer-started school growth
sections.summary: A school started by volunteer professionals and parents with 41 students now serves thousands, helped by MOE, NCSS and SG Enable.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Started by volunteers, professionals who are professionals and also parents.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: We started only with 41 students, and thanks to the Ministry of Education, NCSS and SG Enable, it is now a large and popular school serving thousands.

sections.label: Council roles and agency intersections
sections.summary: The Bill strengthens the Council's functions in coordination, capability development, data use and system stewardship, requiring clarity on how roles and agencies intersect.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: With this Bill strengthening the Council's functions in coordination, capability development, data use and system stewardship, there needs to be clarity on how these roles and agencies intersect.

sections.label: Implementation, compliance and service gaps
sections.summary: Questions are raised on implementing the Bill without compliance-driven behaviour, calibrating requirements to SSA size and capacity, and coordinating critical service gaps.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: How will the Bill be implemented to ensure that stronger governance and funding relationships do not inadvertently encourage compliance-driven behaviour, stifle innovation or add unnecessary layers of bureaucracy within the social service sector?

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: How will compliance and reporting requirements be calibrated to the size, to the capacity and maturity of the SSAs in this sector, so that both large and small SSAs are not overburdened by administrative costs that detract from frontline service delivery?

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: What system and what structured platform will be put in place to sense, to identify, to prioritise, to plan, to coordinate and to resource critical gaps, both existing and emerging, across the sector?

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: How will NCSS and existing agencies work together to ensure that the most significant and urgent service gaps, such as that in adult disability, the impact of technology, artificial intelligence (AI), AI-driven robots, which really kept some of us worried because these technologies will take away some of the jobs that we are trying to create for the disabled, for the elderly.

sections.label: SSAs and NCSS membership
sections.summary: Many SSAs or Social Purpose Entities are NCSS members, and many social service professionals depend on NCSS for growth and development.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
sentences.text: Many SSAs or Social Purpose Entities are members of NCSS and many social service professionals are dependent on NCSS for their growth and development.

sections.label: NCSS Board representation and engagement
sections.summary: With over 500 NCSS members, Board representation must be deliberate for diverse expertise, and NCSS engaged members on the amendments' rationale.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
sentences.text: Given the NCSS has more than 500 members currently, representation on the Board has to be deliberate and intentional for a diverse range of expertise and perspectives.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
sentences.text: I am truly appreciative that NCSS really took time to engage member organisations to explain the rationale of the amendments, including transitioning to a fully-appointed Council and to consider feedback from the ground to retain membership.

sections.label: Sustainability of social service sector
sections.summary: Speaker hopes NCSS will shape a sustainable, cohesive sector supporting ground-up initiatives and attracting next-generation social service professionals.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
sentences.text: On the sustainability of the social service sector, I am hopeful for NCSS to go further in shaping a sector that is not only responsive and cohesive, but also sustainable, supporting emerging ground-up initiatives and appealing, more importantly, to the next generation of social service professionals who choose a meaningful pathway and a career that is impactful.

sections.label: NCSS support for new SSAs
sections.summary: Speaker hopes NCSS extends beyond members, supports new SSAs, and gives social service professionals elevated access to growth support.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
sentences.text: As sector developers, I hope for NCSS to continue to extend your ambit beyond your members, as has earlier been mentioned, and to support newly established SSAs to grow its impact sustainably.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
sentences.text: Social service professionals should have elevated access to support for growth and development, to remain ahead of the curve and be equipped to support emerging needs of beneficiaries.

sections.label: Refreshed mandate and professional pathways
sections.summary: Speaker hopes the refreshed mandate brings more pathways and specialised post-secondary courses, strengthening Singapore's social service ecosystem.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
sentences.text: Taking inspiration from how the Ministry has professionalised and continues to do so with the early childhood industry, I am hopeful that the refreshed mandate will also see more pathways for aspiring professionals in social impact, particularly specialised courses at post-secondary level.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
sentences.text: With NCSS operating with a refreshed mandate, I am hopeful this Bill will strengthen Singapore's social service ecosystem, nurturing a sector that is capable, connected, diverse and aligned with the needs of the people it serves.

sections.label: Wage guideline harmonisation timeline
sections.summary: Speaker asks the Minister to confirm the first quarter 2026 timeline for wage-guideline harmonisation and NCSS's facilitative role.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: At a recent dialogue, the union side proposed to harmonise community care and social services wage guidelines and recommendations, precisely because inconsistent approaches, such as "basic versus gross", as I mentioned earlier, can distort benchmarking.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: I understand that the goal discussed was to have harmonisation in place by first quarter 2026 before moving into accreditation, not just for the Community Care Organisations but also for SSAs.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Could the Minister confirm whether the first quarter in 2026 remains the intended timeline for wage-guideline harmonisation and whether NCSS will play a facilitative role, given its new function to establish and maintain standards and guidelines for sector members?

sections.label: Wage benchmarks and workforce pillars
sections.summary: Speaker lists wage benchmarks, workforce development, manpower productivity, and progressive employment practices as areas to address.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: First, wage benchmarks, referencing MOH salary guidelines; second, workforce development and skills enhancement aligned to Agency for Integrated Care skills standards/skills framework; third, manpower productivity, including job redesign and use of grants; and fourth, progressive employment practices – tripartite standards and fair employment practices should be in place.

sections.label: Accreditation approach for NCSS
sections.summary: Speaker asks whether NCSS will support an accreditation approach with wage benchmarks and workforce development, extended beyond community care.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: If NCSS is to be a sector developer, then I would ask, can the Minister share whether NCSS will support an accreditation approach that includes wage benchmarks and workforce development as central pillars and whether this can be extended beyond community care to social service agencies, in line with the earlier discussions?

sections.label: NCSS standards and sector member safeguards
sections.summary: MP asks how NCSS will keep standards proportionate for smaller agencies and what safeguards ensure fair decisions on sector members.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Could the Minister clarify how NCSS will ensure that standards and reporting requirements are proportionate, particularly for the smaller agencies and charities that may not have the same administrative capacity?

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Relatedly, the Bill also allows NCSS to consider whether an organisation's aims, objects and activities are contrary to the public interest, public order or national harmony when deciding whether to appoint or revoke a sector member.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: I would ask the Minister to elaborate on the safeguards and due processes in place to ensure decisions remain fair, transparent and consistent, particularly given that sector members status will likely be important for participation and sector coordination.

sections.label: NCSS job quality and salary guidelines
sections.summary: MP urges NCSS to focus on job quality and welcomes harmonising salary guidelines before progressive employer accreditation.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: As a sector developer, NCSS needs to focus more decisively on job quality: skills development and career pathways, wage clarity and competitiveness, as well as workplace well-being and psychosocial safety.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: We welcome efforts to harmonise salary guidelines across subsectors, including aligning definitions such as basic wage and gross wage, with clear targets, before moving towards progressive employer accreditation that recognises fair employment practices, training, productivity and worker protection.

sections.label: NCSS membership criteria impact
sections.summary: MP asks how many of the more than 500 NCSS members would be impacted by narrowing membership criteria.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: Any cost savings for our social service agencies should be regarded as a beneficial outcome.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: That said, I would like to ask, out of the more than 500 current NCSS members, how many members would be impacted by this move to narrow the membership criteria of the reconstituted Council?

sections.label: Council maximum size reasons
sections.summary: MP asks the reasons behind setting a large maximum Council size, despite the Council keeping to 23 members.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: While the Minister has stated quite clearly that the Council will keep to 23 members in that immediate term, I would like to ask, what were the reasons behind setting such a large maximum size of the Council?

sections.label: Appeals for section 11 decisions
sections.summary: MP asks whether other administrative decisions under section 11(2) and (3) would also be open to formal appeals.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: As the NCSS takes on an expanded role as the sector developer, which encompasses a larger social service mission beyond membership, I would like to ask if the other administrative decisions, as laid out under section 11, subsections (2) and (3) of the Bill, would also be open to similar formal appeals to the Minister.

sections.label: ComChest grant recipients transition
sections.summary: MP asks whether enhanced governance framework changes affect current ComChest grant recipients and if a transition period exists.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: Will changes to the enhanced governance framework for the ComChest impact current grant recipients and, if so, will there be a transition period for such recipients to improve their processes in order to qualify for continued grants?

sections.label: NCSS capability building initiatives
sections.summary: Between 2015 and 2025, NCSS introduced the Social Service Institute, launched the ComChest integrated fundraising model and developed sector-wide capability frameworks.

sentences.speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Between 2015 and 2025, NCSS introduced the Social Service Institute to build professional capability, launched the ComChest integrated fundraising model and developed sector-wide capability frameworks in areas, such as digitalisation, volunteer management, governance, fundraising and programme evaluation.

sections.label: Ageing population and resourcing challenges
sections.summary: By 2035, ageing and smaller intergenerational households may require rethinking care models, with charities facing tighter fundraising and manpower constraints.

sentences.speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: By 2035, Singapore's ageing population and the shrinking size of intergenerational households may necessitate a fundamental rethinking of care models.

sentences.speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Over the next two decades, the resourcing landscape will continue to evolve, with charities facing tighter fundraising conditions and manpower constraints, exacerbated by competition with the healthcare sector and regional labour markets.

sections.label: NCSS annual accountability reports
sections.summary: The question asks whether NCSS will continue publishing annual accountability reports on financial decisions, reporting metrics and audit findings.

sentences.speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Will NCSS continue publishing annual accountability reports that set out major ﬁnancial decisions, reporting metrics against its expanded mandate, and audit ﬁndings relating to these funds?

sections.label: NCSS as sector conductor
sections.summary: NCSS is described as a conductor, not the loudest instrument, and the Bill strengthens its ability to conduct the sector.

sentences.speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: If our social service sector is much like an orchestra made of many skilled and committed players, then NCSS is not meant to play the loudest instrument.

sentences.speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Rather, it is the conductor, setting the tempo, ensuring harmony and allowing each organisation to contribute its strengths at the right moment.

sentences.speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: When the conductor does its job well, the music belongs to everyone.

sentences.speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: This Bill strengthens NCSS’s ability to play that role.

sentences.speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: NCSS should conduct the sector and not dominate it.

sections.label: NCSS role as sector developer
sections.summary: The Bill formalises NCSS's role as sector developer of Singapore's social service sector.

sentences.speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The Bill formalises NCSS’ role as sector developer of Singapore’s social service sector.

sections.label: Social worker caseloads and anxiety
sections.summary: Social workers handle 20 to 50 cases at one time and crisis outside usual hours, and a SUSS survey found over half suffered anxiety.

sentences.speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Social workers have been known to handle 20 to 50 cases at one time and often handle crisis outside usual working hours.

sentences.speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: During the pandemic, when their help was most needed, it is concerning to learn that in a Singapore University for Social Sciences (SUSS) survey, over half of social workers surveyed suffered from anxiety.

sections.label: Board members appointed by Minister
sections.summary: Under the section 5 amendment, all Board members would be appointed by the Minister for Social and Family Development instead of having some elected members.

sentences.speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Under the section 5 amendment, all Board members would be appointed by the Minister for Social and Family Development instead of having some elected members.

sections.label: Social worker caseloads and sustainability
sections.summary: A Member notes heavy social worker caseloads and COVID-19 anxiety, welcomes the Council's sustainability objective, and asks what actions the Minister will take.

sentences.speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Some social workers may handle 20, or even 50 cases simultaneously and often need to deal with emergency situations outside office hours.

sentences.speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: A survey by the Singapore University of Social Sciences found that during COVID-19, more than half of the social workers surveyed faced anxiety issues, which is concerning.

sentences.speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I am heartened that the authorities have recognised this situation and included the sustainability of the social service sector as one of the Council's statutory objectives in this Bill.

sentences.speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Can the Minister further explain what actions will be taken to achieve this objective?

sections.label: Bill codifies NCSS role
sections.summary: The Bill codifies NCSS's role as a sector developer and strengthens delivery of social services to underserved groups in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cai Yinzhou (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Recognising the importance of SSAs in providing support to Singaporeans and Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cai Yinzhou (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: This Bill codifies the role of NCSS as a sector developer and strengthens the delivery of social services to underserved groups in Singapore.

sections.label: Board size and sector representation
sections.summary: Public consultation indicated sector representation on the Board is a priority, and the proposed Board size is increased to 15-27 members, half appointed by the Minister from sector nominations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cai Yinzhou (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: The public consultation on these amendments, conducted by MSF and NCSS indicated that ensuring sector representation on the Board is a priority.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cai Yinzhou (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: I commend the Ministry for taking this feedback into account and increasing the proposed Board size to 15-27 members and ensuring that half of the Board will be appointed by the Minister from sector members’ nominations.

sections.label: Social enterprises and NCSS registration
sections.summary: A Member asks whether social enterprises can register as NCSS members and how NCSS and raiSE differ in supporting social enterprises.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cai Yinzhou (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: In line with the vision of expanding NCSS' role as sector developer, I would like to ask whether social enterprises will be eligible to register as members under NCSS or, if not, how NCSS plans to provide greater support for our social enterprises.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cai Yinzhou (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Additionally, could the Ministry clarify the distinction between NCSS and raiSE, in terms of the functions they will play in supporting social enterprises?

sections.label: Council objectives and sector direction
sections.summary: The amendments articulate the Council's objectives to build an effective, efficient and sustainable social service sector, positioning it as a sector developer rather than merely a coordinating body.

sentences.speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: By explicitly articulating the Council's objectives, which is to build an effective, efficient and sustainable social service sector, the amendments provide important direction not just to the Council, but also to organisations working closely with it, particularly in a sector where resources are finite and expectations often high.

sentences.speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: Social service work today requires not only compassion, but strong governance, professional competencies and cross-sector collaboration.

sentences.speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: These amendments help position the Council as a sector developer, rather than merely a coordinating body.

sections.label: Support for smaller community organisations
sections.summary: The speaker hopes smaller community-based organisations do not lose membership status and resources, suggesting a graduated approach with differentiated requirements, transition periods and capacity-building support.

sentences.speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: I hope that this would not cause these smaller community-based organisations to lose their membership status and, as a result, do not get resources allocated to them to serve these smaller groups in our population.

sentences.speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: So, it would be prudent for the Council to adopt a graduated and supportive approach, such as perhaps, differentiated requirements, clearly defined transition periods and capacity-building support to those who need it.

sections.label: Council powers and financial provisions
sections.summary: The speaker trusts the Council's power will be exercised judiciously, and welcomes strengthened financial provisions and a more robust framework for long-term sustainability.

sentences.speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: While this is understandable, given the Council's role in implementing Government policy, I trust that this power will continue to be exercised judiciously, preserving the Council's ability to engage openly with the sector and to provide frank policy advice grounded in operational realities.

sentences.speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: By clarifying its role in mobilising financial and in-kind resources, including volunteer support, the Bill reinforces the ComChest's position as a vital bridge between philanthropy and social needs.

sentences.speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: The updated governance framework will help maintain donor confidence while ensuring alignment with the Council's broader objectives.

sentences.speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: I also welcome the strengthened financial provisions, including those relating to funds, investments and the endowment fund.

sentences.speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: As social needs grow more complex, financial resilience and stewardship will be increasingly important and these amendments provide a more robust framework for long-term sustainability.

sentences.speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: It equips NCSS with clearer authority, stronger governance and a more strategic mandate, while also reminding us of the need to balance oversight with partnership and accountability with trust.

sections.label: NCSS as statutory sector developer
sections.summary: The Bill formally positions NCSS as the statutory sector developer for social services.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: At its core, this Bill formally positions NCSS as the statutory sector developer for social services.

sections.label: Sector-nominated Council appointments
sections.summary: The Bill requires at least half of the Council, excluding the Chairperson, to be appointed from individuals nominated by sector members.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: The Bill requires that at least half of the Council, excluding the Chairperson, to be appointed from individuals nominated by sector members.

sections.label: Sector members and prescribed standards
sections.summary: The Bill introduces sector members and requires compliance with prescribed standards for management, administration, service provision and cooperation with NCSS.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: The Bill introduces "sector members" and requires compliance with prescribed standards for management, administration, service provision and cooperation with NCSS in section 15(4).

sections.label: Uneven digitalisation capacity across agencies
sections.summary: NCSS' Industry Digital Plan for Social Services highlighted uneven capacity across agencies, particularly in digitalisation and capability building.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: NCSS' own Industry Digital Plan for Social Services has highlighted uneven capacity across agencies, particularly in digitalisation and capability building.

sections.label: Proportionate, tiered approach explained
sections.summary: It means all agencies meet clear baseline requirements for safety, governance and accountability, with additional compliance scaled to size, risk and complexity.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Allow me to clarify what does "proportionate, tired approach" means.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: It means ensuring that all agencies meet clear baseline requirements for safety, governance and accountability, while scaling additional compliance and obligations according to an agency's size, risk profile and service complexity.

sections.label: NCSS revocation and appeals
sections.summary: The Bill lets NCSS revoke sector-member appointments, with appeals to the Minister within 14 days and the Minister's decision final.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: The Bill allows NCSS to revoke sector-member appointments, with appeals to the Minister within 14 days, and with Minister's decision being final.

sections.label: Publishing sector-level indicators
sections.summary: It suggests publishing sector-level indicators such as service access, timeliness, satisfaction, outcomes, workforce retention and training uptake.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Without oversimplifying complex social outcomes, it may be useful to publish sector-level indicators such as service access and timeliness, aggregated service-user satisfaction and outcomes, and workforce retention and training uptake.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: They are a vital pillar of the "we first" society as we seek to strengthen.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: This Bill strengthens our ability to go together, through clearer stewardship, clearer standards, stronger coordination and modern governance.

sections.label: Minister appoints Chairperson and Council
sections.summary: Under the new section 5, the Minister appoints the Chairperson and the Council, with at least seven nominees from the sector.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Under the new section 5, the Minister appoints the Chairperson and the Council, with at least seven nominees from the sector.

sections.label: Minister directions not disclosed
sections.summary: Under clause 10(6), the Minister may issue directions which the Council must not disclose.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Under clause 10(6), the Minister may issue directions which the Council "must not disclose".

sections.label: Council objectives not court-enforceable
sections.summary: Clause 11(4) states the Council's objectives do not impose any duty on the Council enforceable in a court of law.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Clause 11(4) explicitly states that the objectives of the Council "do not impose any duty on the Council enforceable in a court of law".

sections.label: NCSS membership revocation power
sections.summary: New section 15(6) lets NCSS revoke membership if an organisation acts contrary to the public interest.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Clause 10, under new section 15(6), empowers NCSS to revoke membership if an organisation acts "contrary to the public interest".

sections.label: Learning from failure capability
sections.summary: A member asks for explicit sector-wide learning from serious case reviews and a near-miss reporting system.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Fourth, on capabilities under section 11(2)(f), the most vital capability is learning from failure.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Should there not be an explicit requirement to turn every serious case review into sector-wide learning?

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: We also need a "near-miss" reporting system, similar to aviation, so the whole body learns when one part fails.

sections.label: Members' views on Bill
sections.summary: Members broadly welcomed the Bill's intent to strengthen NCSS and asked for governance, workforce development and sector voice.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Members have broadly welcomed the Bill's intent to strengthen NCSS as a sector developer, while consistently emphasising shared priorities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Members have also asked for stronger governance and workforce development to go hand-in-hand with meaningful sector voice.

sections.label: Who qualifies as members
sections.summary: Organisations must primarily provide or directly support social services in Singapore; all Full Council Members become sector members.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: On whom will qualify, an organisation must have the primary function of providing or directly supporting the provision of a social service in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: Today, there are about 400 Full Council Members and close to 100 Associate Council Members.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: With the changes, all Full Council Members will be transitioned to become sector members.

sections.label: Appointed Council and representation
sections.summary: Appointment replaces elections for the NCSS Board, with at least half the Council from sector members' nominations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: Unlike the previous elections system for the NCSS Board, an appointment approach gives us greater certainty that we can constitute the Council with people from various backgrounds, including candidates from organisations of different sizes and nature, and with the necessary range of skills and experiences.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: We have provided that at least half of the Council, excluding the Chairperson, must come from sector members' nominations, as a clear indication of our commitment to ensure that the sector is represented on the Council.

sections.label: Council size comparison
sections.summary: The range is comparable to other Statutory Boards like the National Arts Council and National Heritage Board, based on needs of the time.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: The range is comparable to that of the allowed size of other Statutory Boards that play similar roles in their sectors, like the National Arts Council and the National Heritage Board, and the eventual size will be based on the needs of the time.

sections.label: Serving out current term
sections.summary: The intent is for them to serve out their current term until 31 July 2026.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: Practically, our intent is for them to serve out their current term, that is, until 31 July 2026.

sections.label: NCSS caregiver and sustainability grants
sections.summary: NCSS introduced the Income OrangeAid Caregiver Support Accelerator Grant with Income Insurance Limited, and supports SSAs through the SG60 Towards Sustainability Fund.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: For example, NCSS recently introduced the Income OrangeAid Caregiver Support Accelerator Grant, in partnership with Income Insurance Limited, to encourage SSAs and their partners to develop solutions to strengthen support for caregivers in Singapore – an important area of need that we are seeing.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: NCSS also supports SSAs in measuring the effectiveness of their programmes through the SG60 Towards Sustainability Fund, which provides funding and capability building support.

sections.label: Sabbatical leave and care fund
sections.summary: NCSS introduced a Sabbatical Leave Scheme offering 10 weeks of paid leave, and MSF and NCSS will set up a Protection Practitioners Care Fund.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: For example, NCSS introduced the Sabbatical Leave Scheme, which offers eligible professionals a chance to rejuvenate with 10 weeks of paid sabbatical leave.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: Moving forward, MSF and NCSS will be setting up a Protection Practitioners Care Fund to implement capability building and well-being initiatives for protection practitioners.

sections.label: NCSS engagement at AGM
sections.summary: NCSS first formally engaged the sector on the proposed amendments at its AGM in July 2024.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: NCSS first formally engaged the sector on the proposed amendments at its AGM in July 2024.

sections.label: Formalising NCSS sector developer role
sections.summary: Formalising NCSS' expanded role as Sector Developer lets it consult widely, identify ground needs and coordinate with stakeholders, and the citation "2025" will change to "2026".

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: By formalising NCSS' expanded role as Sector Developer, NCSS is better able to consult more widely, identify ground needs and closely partner and coordinate with stakeholders to develop the social service sector.

sentences.speaker: The Chairman
sentences.text: The citation here "2025" will be changed to "2026" as indicated in the Order Paper Supplement.
